# Design objective

Make the paper's REPAIR estimator usable without asking an analyst to assemble
error arrays manually. Keep the MLM fixed while the structural
model changes, and make each analysis person's predictions, covariance, and inclusion
status inspectable. Use **MLM** and **structural model**, since
“level 1/level 2” is ambiguous for a multilevel MLM.

This document supersedes the October 20 outline. It describes the implementation,
not an aspirational interface. The source is canonical; the obsolete outline PDF
has been removed. The [audit](design-audit.md) records findings and decisions.

For current model/inference limits and practical help, use the
[support guide](../vignettes/support-and-troubleshooting.Rmd). The
[release-hardening audit](release-hardening.md) records installed-help, teaching-data,
citation, and persistence decisions; the [release checklist](release-checklist.md)
separates preparation from publishing a versioned artifact.

# Analyst workflow

1. Fit and inspect a Gaussian `lmer()` or linear `lme()` model using its native interface.
2. Name the fit in `models = list(growth = growth_fit)`.
3. Call `repair_effects(models)` to discover scalar coefficient names and groups.
4. Specify one additive structural formula, such as
   `outcome ~ re("time", model = "growth") + age`.
5. Supply one structural-data row per ID and an explicit ID column name.
6. Optionally call `repair_data()` to inspect scope matching and error inputs.
7. Call `repair()`; use `summary()`, `coef()`, `vcov()`, `confint()`, and `nobs()`.
   For reporting and joins, use `repair_coefficients()`, `repair_predictions()`, and
   `repair_prediction_covariance()` with their documented table identities.
8. Inspect `repair_reliability(fit)` and `repair_diagnostics(fit)` for reliability,
   scope accounting, measurement messages, and numerical diagnostics. Select
   individual diagnostic tables with `table = "name"`. Plot
   unit-level reliability to inspect heterogeneity.

# Supported scope

One equation, Gaussian lmer or linear lme MLMs with one target grouping factor each,
additive predictors, and an intercept. Random coefficients can appear on either
side. Observed predictors can be numeric, logical, or factors; an observed
outcome must be numeric. A named list can supply several fits to the equation.
Multiple referenced models require explicit independent prediction errors or supplied
per-ID covariance blocks for every model pair. Grouping names can differ; person
identity must agree across fits. See `multimodel-validation.md`.

Single-group nlme prediction extraction and structural fitting now support independent, AR(1),
and continuous-time AR(1) correlation, with constant, varIdent, or varPower
residual variance. Effective rows, fitted contrasts, and residual covariance are
validated; see `nlme-validation.md`. Multilevel nlme extraction is rejected.
lmer nuisance groups may be contained within targets: every fitted nuisance
level must belong to one target level on all effective rows. The same covariance
enters prediction extraction and posterior reliability; see `nested-nuisance-validation.md`.
Shared nuisance groups remain rejected because their cross-person prediction-error
covariance cannot enter the row-wise M-MOM contract. Multilevel nlme remains unsupported.

# Contracts and responsibilities

## Effect identity and formula parsing

Identity is `(model, group, scalar coefficient)`. `re()` accepts literal strings;
model and target-group qualification are optional only when unambiguous. Each
model selects exactly one target group. Existing single-group labels are preserved;
labels from multi-group models include the group. `(Intercept)` is canonical;
`1` and `Intercept` are input aliases. Generated columns use reserved `.repair_`
names so observed columns cannot mask predictions. Output labels retain model identity.

The parser validates a small grammar without evaluating marker arguments.
Interactions, nonlinear score transformations, offsets, `.`, no-intercept models,
and multiple equations fail explicitly. Outcome/predictor identity is checked.
Observed transformations must be precomputed in the unit-level data frame.

## Measurement extraction and prediction extraction

`class_mlm_elements` is the backend normalization contract. The existing scorer
returns `class_repair_ranef`, with lists keyed by group:

- `predictions`: ID by coefficient matrix;
- `prediction_error_covariance`: coefficient by coefficient by ID array;
- `levels`, `terms`, and per-group/per-cluster diagnostics.

Independent lme4 blocks for one group (including `||`) are normalized into
level-major design columns and block-diagonal random covariance. Repeated
coefficient names within a group are rejected as ambiguous for prediction extraction.

The structural workflow always requests deviations (`include_fixed = FALSE`).
Likelihood-only prediction extraction subtracts fixed effects and offsets and uses the fitted
residual covariance (including prior weights). Failed score blocks remain
missing, with diagnostic reasons. They are not silently replaced by BLUPs.

## Assembly and validation

`repair_data()` is the sole assembly boundary. The supplied data frame defines
the scope and order. IDs match model grouping levels as strings, never by row
position. Duplicate/missing/empty IDs always fail. All needed observed variables
must exist. Long data are not implicitly aggregated.

Default missingness policy is failure. Explicit `na_action = "omit"` warns and
records ID/reason rows for absent MLM IDs, nonfinite/missing observed
values, or failed prediction extraction. Extra MLM IDs are recorded separately. The
analysis matrix is checked for adequate sample size and full column rank.

`class_repair_data` holds IDs, formula, outcome, predictor matrix, error arrays,
effect mapping, full score result, and diagnostics. Its validator checks aligned
dimensions and unique IDs. M-MOM further validates finite values and positive
semidefinite joint covariance. Every score selection/permutation is applied to
both axes of its covariance block. Observed columns get zero error; within-model
cross-covariance is preserved, including `err_xy`. Cross-model blocks are aligned
by model name, coefficient name, and ID, then checked jointly for positive
semidefiniteness. Missing supplied blocks are errors, not omission candidates.
Single-model `@predictions` remains a prediction object; multiple-model `@predictions` is a named
list. Diagnostics always include `mlm_models` and `cross_model_error`.

## Estimation and output

`repair()` delegates assembly to `repair_data()` and estimation to `fit_mmom()`.
It returns the existing `class_repair_mod` extended with `analysis_data` and `call`.
Only referenced MLMs are retained. `struc_fit` remains the stable
M-MOM fit/failure class. Numerical failures warn and remain inspectable; standard
coefficient/covariance accessors refuse failed fits.

The public `regularization` setting applies to both moment steps. Minimum uses
q + 2; custom requires an explicit constant at least q + 2; none disables
stabilization while retaining measurement-error subtraction. Advanced users can
set the two controls independently through `fit_mmom()`.

Summaries show effect sources, requested/analyzed/excluded people, coefficient
inference, regularization and actual subtraction multipliers, MLM
messages and singularity, selected-effect posterior reliability, weight
concentration, and the conditional normal-inference convention.
`nobs()` means analyzed units. `confint()` can change the confidence level.

# Methodological boundaries

The covariance uses the final modified moment for its bread, preliminary slopes
for the extra error term, and squared inverse case-variance weights in that term.
It conditions on estimated MLM parameters and assumes the
model-based normal-error covariance and independent analysis people. It is not
robust inference and does not account for MLM parameter estimation.

`dev/target_grouping_vars.Rmd` describes a target-specific *within-cluster*
covariance. That is necessary but insufficient to justify independent structural
rows when target clusters share nuisance levels. Containment now supplies the supported special case where these cross-cluster
blocks are zero under the fitted model. Cross-cluster covariance and its downstream
estimator must be specified before admitting shared nuisance levels.

# Development workflow and acceptance gates

1. Define the effect identities, statistical estimand, and error-covariance
   contract before adding syntax or a backend.
2. Implement normalization/prediction extraction and verify against independently calculated
   predictions and covariance, including effective observation order and missingness.
3. Extend assembly with explicit matching and failure policies; test covariance
   permutations and selected outcome/predictor cross-terms.
4. Connect the estimator without changing its scientific target implicitly.
5. Add executable examples, help, a capability boundary, and diagnostic output.
6. Run the existing manuscript/simulation fixtures for R and C++ backends, new
   integration tests, README/vignette execution, and a source-package check.
7. Document any remaining check warnings and methodological limits in the PR.

The single-group nlme effective-row and residual-covariance validation milestone
is implemented (see `nlme-validation.md`), as is the multiple-model assembly
contract (see `multimodel-validation.md`). Reliability and structural diagnostic
interfaces are now implemented with explicit contrast, scope, aggregation, and
undefined-value contracts; see `reliability-validation.md`. Stable table extractors
are implemented; see `extractor-contracts.md` for schema and compatibility rules.
Cross-platform automated checks are now configured; see `ci-checks.md` for the
matrix, warning policy, artifacts, and local reproduction. A pkgdown website now
organizes the executable guides and reference, with PR validation and main-branch
GitHub Pages deployment; see `website.md`. Bootstrap inference,
additional residual structures, and shared-group dependence validation require
separate validation. Cross-unit covariance support and formula extensions with
derived error propagation require explicit statistical contracts.


# Verified refitting (2026-10-30)

`repair_refit()` implements single-model identity replay before explicit
replacement fitting. Original measurement/person data are required; `new_*`
arguments supply replacements. Native data-only lmer/lme recipes and explicit
callbacks preserve observable specifications, effective rows and coefficient
schemas. Structural factor matrices are recorded; refit summaries expose audited
counts, controls, warnings and versions. Deterministic whole-unit draws assign
fresh target/nuisance IDs with an explicit source map. No random sampling or
bootstrap inference is added. See `refitting-validation.md` and the executable
refitting guide for the contract, tests and restrictions.
